clue.text: One member gobbled by broadcaster is inadequate

indicators.note: what is gobbled by something ends up inside it, so the member's letters sit within the broadcaster

parts.note: Sky is the British satellite TV broadcaster
the Roman numeral for one
MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A broadcaster swallowing up a single politician is judged to be falling short.
explanation.definitionFit: Something skimpy is meagre or scant, so inadequate in amount.

clue.text: Embodiment of a country's relations with a Frenchman

parts.note: uncles are family relations
M is the abbreviation for Monsieur, a Frenchman

explanation.surface: A nation's dealings with France are described as if in a foreign-policy column.
explanation.definitionFit: Uncle Sam is the cartoon personification of the United States and its government.

clue.text: The latest throwaway tv transmission…

parts.note: the latest is news, the most recent information
something cast off is thrown away; cast as discarded

explanation.surface: A disposable modern television broadcast, leading on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A newscast is a broadcast bulletin of news on radio or television.

clue.text: … a pisspoor discussion show to almost top 'Hattersley'

indicators.note: almost means the word is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: to top someone is slang for to kill them
Roy Hattersley, Labour politician of the period

explanation.surface: A poor TV discussion programme is accused of nearly finishing off Roy Hattersley.
explanation.walkthrough: Kilroy was the daytime BBC discussion show hosted by Robert Kilroy-Silk; Roy Hattersley was Labour's deputy leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Kilroy was a daytime television talk show where a studio audience debated topical issues.

clue.text: All over the place, these 'E' dropping yobs — they get good commission

indicators.note: letters all over the place are scattered and must be rearranged
dropping says the named letter is taken out of the fodder before rearranging

parts.note: the letter E as named

explanation.surface: Rough lads scattered about, dropping their aitches and getting paid well for it.
explanation.walkthrough: THESE YOBS shuffled, with one E dropped, gives the auction house's name; the 'E' in quotes mimics a cockney dropped aitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Sotheby's is a London auction house that earns a commission on each lot sold.

clue.text: Heckler taken out (name concealed) by government bully-boy

indicators.note: out, as in put out of order, says the letters are rearranged
concealed says the name's letter is hidden in among the rest

explanation.surface: A heckler is removed, his identity hidden, by a government heavy.
explanation.walkthrough: HECKLER and TAKEN with N for name are rearranged into the politician's full name; Kenneth Clarke was then a Cabinet minister known for his combative style.
explanation.definitionFit: Kenneth Clarke was a bruiser of a Conservative Cabinet minister, here cast as the government's enforcer.

clue.text: House to hush-hush Ray's philandering — will he never resign?

parts.note: a house is a home
hush-hush means secret

indicators.note: philandering suggests wandering around, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the name Ray, its 's read as 'is'

explanation.surface: A household hushes up a man's affair, and the question is when the minister will quit.
explanation.definitionFit: The Home Secretary is the UK Cabinet minister for policing and justice, who had faced resignation calls.

clue.text: Miss this West End show!

parts.note: fill in the blank: the musical called Miss ___, playing in London's West End

explanation.walkthrough: The surface tells you to skip a show; really 'Miss' is the first word of the musical's title.
explanation.definitionFit: Miss Saigon was a long-running musical in London's West End theatre district.

clue.text: Practice of surgeons/medics leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the opening letters, taken from each of the two medical words

parts.note: the slash stands between the two letters and is read aloud as the word 'and' set there
the leading letter of medics, under the same 'leaders' instruction

explanation.surface: A routine of surgeons and medics, as if describing a hospital's methods.
explanation.definitionFit: S and M, sadomasochism, is a sexual practice involving inflicting and receiving pain.

clue.text: Undercover items? Just about the last thing you'll find in our mag ()

definitions.meaning: first meaning: underwear, worn under clothes

definitions.text: Just about the last thing you'll find in our mag
definitions.meaning: second meaning: the small ads near the back of Private Eye

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'smalls' is everyday slang for underwear; the magazine's classified ads were also called smalls.
explanation.definitionFit: Smalls means both underclothes and the short classified advertisements printed at the back of a magazine.

clue.text: Norma's around to check final diary entry as a rule

indicators.note: around suggests moving the letters about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the name Norma, John Major's wife
CH is the chess abbreviation for check

indicators.note: final picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Norma Major pops round to look over the last entry in a diary.
explanation.definitionFit: Monarchy is government by a king or queen, a form of rule.

clue.text: Jay mostly pisses 'em off (see some of our back issues)

definitions.text: see some of our back issues

indicators.note: off says the letters are thrown into a new order
mostly says most of the word is kept, here losing its opening letter

parts.note: the name Jay
the word 'em as printed

explanation.surface: Someone called Jay largely annoys people.
explanation.walkthrough: AY (Jay without J) with PISSES and EM are rearranged; Eye's passim is the magazine's tag for 'see many past issues'.
explanation.definitionFit: Passim means throughout, so the tag directs readers to Private Eye's scattered earlier coverage.

clue.text: Some very obscene Eye feature

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rather filthy regular item in the magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: Yobs, hooligans, appear often in Private Eye as a running subject.

clue.text: Such a little thing, but one randy Persian, perhaps

parts.note: one is the article a
a tom is a male cat, known for prowling after mates; a Persian is a breed of cat

explanation.surface: A small creature that is nonetheless a lustful Persian.
explanation.definitionFit: An atom is the smallest unit of an element, proverbially a tiny thing.

clue.text: Seat of foreign government in which shaky Heath gets the sweats and drops one

indicators.note: shaky says the letters wobble into a new order
drops says a letter is let go from the word

parts.note: ague is a fever with sweating and shivering
one is the letter A

explanation.surface: Abroad, a trembling Ted Heath breaks into a sweat and loses something.
explanation.walkthrough: Edward Heath was a former Conservative PM; 'shaky' rearranges HEATH to THEHA, and AGUE drops an A to leave GUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hague is where the Dutch government and parliament sit, though Amsterdam is the capital.

clue.text: Understood Bill's in Bristol

indicators.note: in places the bill inside the other word

parts.note: Bristols is rhyming slang (Bristol City, titty) for breasts, so a Bristol is a tit
AC is an account, a bill; the 's reads as 'is'

explanation.surface: Someone called Bill is in the city of Bristol, and that is taken as read.
explanation.walkthrough: British rhyming slang: Bristol City = titty, so Bristols means breasts.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means implied or understood without being openly stated.

clue.text: They're sending an unwelcome message to Major — perhaps he'll stop

definitions.text: They're sending an unwelcome message to Major

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: Bad news for John Major, who might at last step down.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinion surveys showed the Prime Minister's Conservatives far behind, a bleak signal to Downing Street.

clue.text: However, if second's included it's a pair

indicators.note: included puts the letter inside the other word

parts.note: however means but

explanation.surface: A quibbling remark: add a second and it becomes a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: A bust is a woman's bosom, a pair of breasts in the magazine's schoolboy humour.

clue.text: Runner takes awful shit from the Dalai Lama

parts.note: Zola Budd, the barefoot middle-distance runner

indicators.note: awful says the letters are in a mess and need reordering

explanation.surface: An athlete takes vile abuse from the Tibetan spiritual leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Zola Budd was a famous 1980s runner, notorious for her collision with Mary Decker.
explanation.definitionFit: The Dalai Lama is the spiritual head of Tibetan Buddhism, so an example of a Buddhist.

clue.text: Heseltine's gutless nazi

indicators.note: gutless removes the middle, leaving only the outer parts

parts.note: Michael Heseltine's name with its possessive s

explanation.surface: Heseltine is called a cowardly fascist.
explanation.definitionFit: Rudolf Hess was Hitler's deputy, a leading Nazi.

clue.text: To snog Sweden's premier, hang about

indicators.note: premier means first, so the first letter is taken

parts.note: to mooch is to hang about idly

explanation.surface: An instruction to kiss the Swedish prime minister and then loiter.
explanation.definitionFit: To smooch is to kiss and cuddle, the same as to snog in British slang.

clue.text: Brighteyes singularly intellectual?

parts.note: a bright private eye in the singular: a clever detective, and slang for a smart alec

explanation.walkthrough: Dick is slang for a detective or private eye, so one bright eye becomes a clever dick.
explanation.definitionFit: A clever dick is a British insult for a know-all who shows off their intelligence.

clue.text: See 6
Fashionable couplings when Charles is about

indicators.note: is about puts the first word around the other

parts.note: in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Trendy pairings when Prince Charles is around.
explanation.definitionFit: Chains are linked couplings, series of connected links joining things together.

clue.text: One getting poor Norma in a state, as seen on tv

indicators.note: in puts the one and the shuffled name inside the state

parts.note: PA is Pennsylvania, a US state
one is the letter A

indicators.note: poor suggests the name is in a bad way, needing rearranging

explanation.surface: Someone gets poor Norma Major into a state, as broadcast on television.
explanation.definitionFit: Panorama is the BBC's long-running current affairs programme on television.

clue.text: Feeling randy and mounting ex-PM (no hard on though)

parts.note: mounting something is being on it

indicators.note: no says the letter is left out

parts.note: Edward Heath, former Conservative Prime Minister
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A lusty encounter with a former premier, who fails to rise to the occasion.
explanation.definitionFit: On heat describes a female animal in season, so slangily feeling sexually aroused.

clue.text: Knight needs scrutiny we hear — he wanted socialism with a human face

definitions.text: he wanted socialism with a human face

parts.note: to dub is to knight someone with a sword

indicators.note: we hear says the letters entered match a spoken word, not its spelling

parts.note: a check is an examination or scrutiny, said aloud to give the second syllable of the Czech name

explanation.surface: A knight requires close examination, apparently.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Dubček led the 1968 Prague Spring, promising socialism with a human face.

clue.text: Far from sober style in a leader

indicators.note: far from sober means drunk, so the letters of style stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunken manner in a national leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Boris Yeltsin was Russia's president, a national head of state notorious for drinking.
